sentences.en: The ocean is not our place.
sentences.zh: 海洋并非我们的栖身之所。

sentences.en: We can learn to swim, but it doesn't come naturally.
sentences.zh: 我们可以学会游泳，但这并非天性使然。

sentences.en: They want nothing to do with putting their bodies into water.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不想把身体浸入水中。

sentences.en: It's only humankind's incessant need to explore that drives us into such an unwelcoming environment.
sentences.zh: 正是人类那种永无止境的探索需求，驱使我们进入了这样一个并不友好的环境。

sentences.en: And since our bodies aren't built for it, we must design things that allow us to explore this foreign place.
sentences.zh: 既然我们的身体并非为此而生，我们就必须设计出能让我们探索这片陌生领域的工具。
那是我们的凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: Alexander the Great is said to have descended into the ocean more than 2,000 years ago in a glass barrel.
sentences.zh: 据说亚历山大大帝在两千多年前就曾坐着一个玻璃桶潜入过海洋。

sentences.en: There are various paintings of this event.
sentences.zh: 关于这件事有各种各样的画作。

sentences.en: In one, the Great is being lowered into the ocean by a couple of men in a wooden boat.
sentences.zh: 其中一幅画里，几个人在木船上把这位大帝缓缓放入海中。

sentences.en: He's hunched inside his little barrel, still wearing his crown and robe.
sentences.zh: 他蜷缩在小桶里，头上还戴着王冠，身上披着长袍。

sentences.en: The guys in the boat look to me like they are used to humoring his every whim.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，船上的那些人似乎早已习惯了迁就他的一时兴起。

sentences.en: In some versions of the story, Alexander the Great was not in a barrel, but in a diving bell.
sentences.zh: 在故事的某些版本中，亚历山大大帝坐的不是桶，而是一个潜水钟。

sentences.en: Diving bells have been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 潜水钟已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: Aristotle wrote about them around 300 B.C.
sentences.zh: 亚里士多德在公元前300年左右就曾写到过它们。

sentences.en: And they were often actual bells, like from churches.
sentences.zh: 而且它们往往就是真正的钟，就像教堂里的那种。

sentences.en: To understand how one uses such a thing to aid in an ocean dive, try this quick experiment.
sentences.zh: 为了理解人们如何利用这种东西辅助深海潜水，可以试做一个简单的实验。

sentences.en: Fill up your sink with water and push a cup open and down into the water.
sentences.zh: 在水槽里装满水，把一个杯子开口朝下按进水里。

sentences.en: You'll notice that the cup doesn't fill up all the way.
sentences.zh: 你会发现杯子并没有完全被水填满。

sentences.en: There will be a pocket of breathable air on the inside.
sentences.zh: 里面会留有一团可供呼吸的空气。

sentences.en: Amazingly, this works using giant church bells and the ocean, too.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，用巨大的教堂钟和海洋做实验，原理也是一样的。

sentences.en: Divers could lower a bell into the ocean and use it as a kind of home base,
sentences.zh: 潜水员可以把钟放入海中，把它当作一种大本营，

sentences.en: swimming out and around, searching for sunken treasure,
sentences.zh: 游出去四处搜寻沉船宝藏，

sentences.en: and then popping back into the bell for a few gasps of air.
sentences.zh: 然后再回到钟里喘几口大气。

sentences.en: But it wasn't a good solution.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一个好的解决方案。

sentences.en: The bells were cumbersome, and the divers still couldn't go down very far.
sentences.zh: 这种钟非常笨重，而且潜水员依然无法潜入太深的地方。

sentences.en: The main obstacle to exploring the depths of the ocean has always been the pressure.
sentences.zh: 探索深海的主要障碍一直都是压力。

sentences.en: Well, at 200 feet, your lungs collapse and you die.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在200英尺深的地方，你的肺部会塌陷，然后你就会死亡。

sentences.en: That's Jim Gould telling it like it is.
sentences.zh: 那是吉姆·古尔德在陈述事实。

sentences.en: I'm a professor of biology at Princeton.
sentences.zh: 我是普林斯顿大学的生物学教授。

sentences.en: And he's married to Carol Gould, who we'll also be talking to today.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子是卡罗尔·古尔德，我们今天也会采访她。

sentences.en: She and Jim have written 10 books together.
This is how Jim talks about the first time he met Carol.
sentences.zh: 吉姆是这样描述他第一次见到卡罗尔的情景的。

sentences.en: And there she was, the person I've been looking for all my life.
sentences.zh: 她就站在那里，那正是我一生都在寻找的人。

sentences.en: And it didn't take long from then.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，没过多久我们就走到了一起。

sentences.en: In the mid-1800s, a naturalist named Edward Forbes
sentences.zh: 19世纪中期，一位名叫爱德华·福布斯的博物学家

sentences.en: hypothesized that below 300 fathoms, or about 1,800 feet,
sentences.zh: 推测在300英寻（约1800英尺）以下，

sentences.en: no life could exist in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 海洋中不可能存在任何生命。

sentences.en: And people pretty much believed him.
sentences.zh: 而人们基本上都相信了他的话。

sentences.en: Well, the general thought was that it was just common sense that nothing could live down there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时普遍的看法是，深海里什么都活不了，这简直是常识。

sentences.en: Because the deeper you get, the pressure increases on the living tissues.
sentences.zh: 因为越往深处，活体组织承受的压力就越大。

sentences.en: And it gets darker and darker.
And it just made sense to people.
sentences.zh: 这对人们来说合情合理。

sentences.en: You know, the way we are.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是我们人类的思维方式。

sentences.en: So, anthropocentric, if people can't live down there, well, probably nothing else can.
sentences.zh: 太以自我为中心了，如果人类无法在深海生存，那大概其他生物也无法生存。

sentences.en: But these anthropocentric naysayers would soon be proven wrong.
sentences.zh: 但这些以自我为中心的怀疑论者很快就会被证明是错的。

sentences.en: The continents were about to be strung together with telegraph wires.
sentences.zh: 当时各大洲即将通过电报线连接起来。

sentences.en: Starting in 1858, nations were connected with extremely long wires.
sentences.zh: 从1858年开始，各国之间通过极长的电缆连接在一起。

sentences.en: Messages would travel great distances through cables that lay on the ocean floor.
sentences.zh: 信息通过铺设在海底的电缆进行远距离传输。

sentences.en: And in 1860, as the Mediterranean cable was raised for repair from about 6,000 feet,
sentences.zh: 1860年，当人们把地中海电缆从约6000英尺深的海底拉上来维修时，

sentences.en: lo and behold, attached to the cable were critters.
sentences.zh: 瞧，电缆上竟然附着着一些小生物。

sentences.en: Mostly dead critters, but critters that were once alive.
sentences.zh: 大多是死掉的生物，但它们确实曾经活着。

sentences.en: This discovery was much talked about in the press.
sentences.zh: 这一发现引起了媒体的热议。

sentences.en: There was life in the depths of the ocean, and everyone wanted to know more about it.
sentences.zh: 深海中确实存在生命，每个人都想了解更多。

执行最早的科学考察任务之一。

sentences.zh: 那是一艘挂着风帆的巨大而美丽的船。

sentences.zh: 或者纹在二头肌上的那种船。

sentences.en: The scientists and sailors spent four years on this ship,
sentences.zh: 科学家和水手们在这艘船上度过了四年，

sentences.en: studying the Earth's oceans, trying especially to understand the deepest depths.
sentences.zh: 研究地球的海洋，尤其试图了解最深的海域。

sentences.en: And they did things like put down nets very deep into the water and go along,

sentences.en: But just like our bodies can't survive the pressure at great depths,

sentences.en: So as they come up, they basically crystallize and fracture.
sentences.zh: 所以当它们被拉上来时，基本上会结晶并破碎。

sentences.en: So every cell explodes, rather than the whole animal.

sentences.en: Every cell explodes, and what you have is a bag of goo.
